I just upgraded to 2.13 and am unable to reproduce your behavior. Run
works fine on my system. For those that experience the problem, I have
a couple questions for those experiencing the issue which could help
me track down the issue.

1. Are you able to plot from the command line (i.e. plot(1:10))

2. What do you get for the following:
sessionInfo()
Sys.info()
.libPaths()
J("java.lang.System")$getProperties()

3. Clear out your preferences (located in your home directory). On the
mac this is done with:

rm ~/.JGRprefsrc
rm ~/.JGREditorprefsrc
rm ~/.DeducerPrefs

4. Try reinstalling from CRAN:
install.packages(c("JGR","Deducer","rJava","iplots","JavaGD"))

5. Try upgrading to the versions on R forge with:
install.packages(c("JGR","Deducer","rJava"),,"http://www.rforge.net",type="source")

ian

----------------------------------------------------------
Hi,

Several users on the Deducer list have experienced crashes when
plotting ( http://groups.google.com/group/deducer/browse_thread/thread/49d2d65b2db919df
). I've determined that it is not deducer related, and am able to
reproducibly crash my machine without Deducer loaded with the
following code:

data(mtcars)
library(ggplot2)
ggplot() + geom_histogram(aes(x=mpg),data=mtcars)

Though interestingly, the following does not crash JGR:

data(mtcars)
library(ggplot2)
ggplot() + geom_point(aes(x=mpg,y=cyl),data=mtcars)

The crash is reported as an invalid memory access:

Invalid memory access of location 0x10 rip=0x1218c331e

Segmentation fault

I tried with both the rJava available on cran, and the latest rforge
version. Perhaps this is related to the infinite recursion bug I
reported last month (
https://www.rforge.net/bugzilla/show_bug.cgi?id=222 ).

Any thoughts?

Best,
Ian

messages.subject_clean: JGR / R 2.13 / Mac OS X crashes
messages.body_plain:
Hi All,

So it turns out that the crashes that were experienced go all the way
down to the compiler (gcc) used to create the R 2.13 mac binaries.

For those interested here is what happened:
R 2.13 adds some new multi-threaded features to R (GOMP), but
unfortunately GOMP support is broken in gcc 4.2
(http://gcc.gnu.org/bugzilla/show_bug.cgi?id=36242). This caused a
crash whenever R entered multi-threaded code. For example a simple
call to scale(mtcars) would crash JGR. Note that this bug can also
affect linux users if they compile R with gcc 4.2.

The solution:
The next version of R will solve the issue, but in the mean time, mean
time mac users should upgrade to the patched version of R available at
http://r.research.att.com/ .
Direct link: http://r.research.att.com/R-2.13-branch-leopard.pkg

Ian

install correctly for 64-bit R if you try to install it from CRAN
(either directly or via the JGR package installation).

fine under 64-bit R.

I'm indebted to Alberto Mirisola for his wonderful 'PlugInScaling'
package. Thank you very much. However, there's a bug in the Factor
Analysis tool included in it:

If you choose the principal components extraction method, the argument
nfactors passed on to principal() is just void. This is the line
called when the dialog is run:

> pr.model1<-principal(pr.model, nfactors=  , rotate= "promax" )

Therefore, just one component (default option) is extracted,
regardless of what you entered in the dialog. With other extraction
methods (at least with 'maximum likelihood') it works fine.

Helios

messages.body_plain:
Thanks, Alberto.

By the way, if this suggestion arrives on time, have you also
considered to include a request for the scores matrix (i.e.
scores=TRUE in the call to both 'principal' and 'fa')? In my
experience, factor analysis is often a preliminary step for further
analysis of the data, which is done on the simplified subspace of
factor scores, in order to work with a smaller amount of variables. So
it would be very interesting to get the scores matrix in the resulting
'pr.model' object.

Helios
